note: Two layers over one key. kind=exact: b is byte-identical to a, decided by sha256, no threshold involved. kind=near: b is a same-source transform of a, decided by the perceptual layer, so its recall is an upper bound and the threshold is in-sample. label=distinct: two different physical objects (distinct accession numbers in evals/golden-provisional/CREDITS.md), never two photos of one item. Paths are relative to this directory.

pairs.label: duplicate
pairs.transform: byte-for-byte copy (nothing changed, not even the encoding)
pairs.why: the same bytes stored twice: sha256(a) == sha256(b). This pair is decided by the digest layer, so no perceptual threshold can change its verdict.
